rule.name: Remove spaces before certain punctuation, typically . , : ; ? !
rule.description: No space is placed before certain punctuation marks

rule.name: Convert two periods (..) in parenthesis by ellipsis (…)
rule.description: Two consecutive dots in parentheses or brackets most likely indicate an error and should be replaced with an ellipsis

rule.name: Convert all nonbreaking hyphens to regular hyphens
rule.description: Convert all nonbreaking hyphens to regular hyphens and eventually add them later by specific rule

example.before: Coca‑Cola μέσα-έξω πάνω-κάτω
example.after: Coca‑Cola μέσα‑έξω πάνω‑κάτω

rule.name: Two hyphens to en-dash
rule.description: Two hyphens to en-dash

example.before: word -- word number--number
example.after: word – word number–number

rule.name: Convert figure dash to dash between letters
rule.description: Converts figure dash U+2012 into standard dash

example.before: Sapir‒Whorf hypothesis
example.after: Sapir–Whorf hypothesis

rule.name: Remove zero-width characters (U+200B–200D)
rule.description: Remove zero-width spaces, zero-width non-joiner and zero-width joiner to make GREP-based search and replace operations more effective

example.before: www.type​together.com
example.after: www.typetogether.com

rule.name: Em-dash to en-dash
rule.description: Em-dash to en-dash

rule.name: Three or four periods to ellipsis (U+2026)
rule.description: Three or four periods to ellipsis

rule.name: Remove period after certain abbreviations
rule.description: Remove period after certain abbreviations (k.a instead of k.a.)

example.before: Dl. Popescu va sosi la întâlnire cca. la ora 10.
example.after: Dl Popescu va sosi la întâlnire cca la ora 10.

rule.name: Remove all soft hyphens (U+00AD)
rule.description: Remove all soft hyphens (SHY) to make GREP-based search and replace operations more effective

example.before: typo­grafisk
example.after: typografisk

rule.name: Replace two single open quotes ‚ ‚ with one double opening quotation mark „ (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two commas {U+002C} or two low-9 quotation mark (U+201A) double low-9 quotation mark (U+201E)

rule.name: Delete space between quotation marks (hairspace could be added consistently in the next step if required)
rule.description: If primary and secondary quotation marks appear consecutively in the text, no spaces are inserted between them (unless this is a deliberate typographical choice)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes ’ ’ with one double quotation mark ” (correct form of quotation marks to by modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single quotation marks ’’ (U+2019) to double high-9 quotation mark ” (U+201D)

example.before: word’’ (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: word” (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes ‘ ‘ with one double quotation mark “ (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single quotation marks ‘‘ (U+2018) to double high-6 quotation mark “ (U+201C)

example.before: ‘‘word (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: “word (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes ‹ ‹ with one double quotation mark « (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single left-pointing angle quotation ‹‹ (U+2039) to left-pointing double angle quotation « (U+00AB)

example.before: ‹‹word word‹‹ (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: «word word« (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace two single quotes › › with one double quotation mark » (correct form of quotation marks to be modified in next step)
rule.description: Replace two single right-pointing angle quotation ›› (U+203A) to left-pointing double angle quotation » (U+00BB)

example.before: ››word word›› (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)
example.after: »word word» (The change may not be visible, change font style to Typofix EU Special to see the difference)

rule.name: Replace multiple tabs by single tab
rule.description: Multiple tabs are likely a mistake in the text, although they may be part of a legacy table format. In most cases, it is safe to replace them with a single tab (or eventually replace them with a space, or remove them entirely)

category.name: Spaces
Run first – remove extra or double spaces, convert all spaces to standard space (prefs)

example.before: Multiple Tabs ↦↦Multiple Tabs Multiple Tabs↦↦
example.after: Multiple↦Tabs ↦Multiple Tabs Multiple Tabs

rule.name: Remove all kinds of spaces (horizontal and vertical) at the end of the story
rule.description: Removing all vertical and horizontal spaces at the end of a thread.

category.name: Spaces
Run first – remove extra or double spaces, convert all spaces to standard space (prefs)

example.before: This is the end of story. This is the end of story.
example.after: This is the end of story. This is the end of story.

rule.name: Remove spaces adjacent to a tab
rule.description: Spaces next to tabs serve no purpose in the text and should be deleted

category.name: Spaces
Run first – remove extra or double spaces, convert all spaces to standard space (prefs)

example.before: text ↦ text text↦ text text ↦text text ↦
example.after: text↦text text↦text text↦text text↦

rule.name: Ratio / map scale without spaces around colon
rule.description: Remove spaces around colon in ratios (1:100)

rule.name: Delete an extra space at the end of a paragraph
rule.description: A space at the end of a paragraph or article is unnecessary and should be deleted

example.before: Hello! Hello! Hello!↦
example.after: Hello! Hello! Hello!

rule.name: Delete an extra space at the beginning of a paragraph
rule.description: There should be no space at the beginning of a paragraph; any paragraph indentation can be adjusted by setting the paragraph parameters in the application

example.before: Hello! Hi. Ahoj
example.after: Hello! Hi. Ahoj

rule.description: Keep number and large number abbreviations together using nonbreaking space (7 mil.)

example.after: 1 tril., 1 mie, 10 mii

rule.name: Keep number and large number words together using nonbreaking space (30 millions)
rule.description: A numeric value should be connected to a numeral with a non-breaking space to prevent the expression from being split at the end of a line

rule.name: Non-breaking Space in Biblical Book Abbreviations (Tim, 2 Tim etc.)

example.after: 2 Tim. (Dutch, Romanian, English) 1 Împ (Romanian)

rule.name: Non-breaking space in Bible verse reference
rule.description: Bible book, chapter and verse should be connected by non-breaking space so as to avoid splitting the expression at the end of the line

rule.name: Connect numbers up to four digits before closing parenthesis with the last word (final value 11)
rule.description: A number in parentheses should not start the next line, so it is joined to the preceding word with a non-breaking space

example.before: (total value 11) [last number 2001]
example.after: (total value 11) [last number 2001]

rule.name: Thin spaces in three-part abbreviations with periods
rule.description: Replaces normal spaces in abbreviations like s. r. o. by thin spaces

example.before: s. r. l. (Romanian)
example.after: s. r. l. (Romanian)

rule.description: Replaces normal spaces in Czech and Slovak abbreviation spol. s r. o.

example.before: spol. s r. o. spol.s r.o.
example.after: spol. s r. o. spol. s r. o.

rule.name: Narrow spaces in two-part abbreviations with periods

example.before: Firma Dacia s.a. a publicat raportul anual.
example.after: Firma Dacia s. a. a publicat raportul anual.

rule.description: Add missing spaces after closing parenthesis or brackets

rule.name: Replace standard spaces by nonbreaking spaces in numbers
rule.description: Replace standard spaces by nonbreaking spaces (or alternative separators) in numbers. Works only with numbers separated by a regular space into groups of three digits (1 000 000)

rule.name: Use periods for thousand separators instead of spaces
rule.description: Replace spaces by periods in numbers. Works only with numbers separated by a space into groups of three digits (1.000.000)

example.before: This feature must be turned on in preferences 1 000 000 000 000 000 1 000 +420 775 223 197 (to be fixed) 3,141592 (no change) 1974 (no change)
example.after: This feature must be turned on in preferences 1.000.000.000.000.000 1.000,99 +420 775 223 197 (to be fixed) 3,141592 (no change) 1974 (no change)

rule.name: Change any hyphen or dash preceding numbers to minus sign (U+2212) From -2 to −2
rule.description: Hyphens or dashes preceding numbers that are at the beginning of a paragraph, after an opening parenthesis, brackets, braces, or preceded by a space.

example.before: -7, -2,2, –1.2345 –22 + 23 (Czech, Dutch, French, Polish) –22+23 (other languages) (-2), [-2,01234] {—1}
example.after: −7, −2,2, −1.2345 −22 + 23 (Czech, Dutch, French, Polish) –22+23 (other languages) (−2), [−2,01234] {−1}

rule.name: Connect capitalised names with Roman numerals (useful for popes, emperors – Charles IV etc.)
rule.description: The name is joined to the Roman numeral with a non-breaking space to prevent the expression from being split at the end of a line

example.before: Charles IV Johannes Paul II Karl IV Kehä III
example.after: Charles IV Johannes Paul II Karl IV Kehä III

rule.name: Connect suffix after Roman number with nonbreaking hyphen without spaces (XIX-lea)
rule.description: The suffixes following Roman numerals are written with a non-breaking hyphen, without spaces. The non-breaking hyphen prevents the expression from being split at the end of a line

example.before: XIX ‑ lea (Romanian) XIX–lea (Romanian) XIX – a (Romanian)
example.after: XIX‑lea (Romanian) XIX‑lea (Romanian) XIX‑a (Romanian)

rule.name: Nonbreaking space between abbreviations and Roman numbers (Nr. XVI)
rule.description: There should be a non-breaking space between the abbreviation and the number to prevent the expression from being split at the end of the line

example.before: Nr. MDCCIII (Danish, Lithuanian, Latvian, Romanian) În secolele XVI (Romanian)
example.after: Nr. MDCCIII (Danish, Lithuanian, Latvian, Romanian) În secolele XVI (Romanian)

rule.name: Remove duplicate redundant punctuation before closing parenthesis
rule.description: Commas and semicolons are not repeated and are only placed after parentheses

example.before: Type punctuation (comma,), then save the file. (any language)
example.after: Type punctuation (comma), then save the file. (any language)

rule.name: Add period after certain abbreviations if missing
rule.description: Add period after certain abbreviations if missing (et al > et al.)

example.before: John Newton et al
example.after: John Newton et al.

rule.name: Remove Spanish inverted punctuation in languages other than Spanish
rule.description: Inverted punctuation (¡ ¿ ⸘) is only used at the start of a sentence in Spanish; therefore, it must be removed in other languages.

rule.name: Colon in Bible verse reference 1 Kor 3:18 or Mt 12:43–44
rule.description: For Bible references, the chapter and verse numbers are separated by a colon

example.before: Versetul 1 Cor. 15,26 vorbește despre ultimul vrăjmaș.
example.after: Versetul 1 Cor. 15:26 vorbește despre ultimul vrăjmaș.

rule.name: Replaces two periods by a single period
rule.description: A second period is not repeated at the end of a sentence or phrase. (However, it is possible that the author intended an ellipsis …)

example.after: test ’s (no change) test ‘s’ (quotation marks may change to a version defined in preferences)

rule.name: Primary quotation marks „ ”
rule.description: Replace the primary quotation marks in the text with the „ ” style

example.before: "Quotes!" "Quotes and 'inside' quotes." Converting “quotes”. »Converting quotes.«
example.after: „Quotes!" „Quotes and 'inside' quotes.“ Converting „quotes“. „Converting quotes.“

rule.name: Secondary quotation marks « »

example.after: ’Cześć!’ Say ’good bye’. ’Ich bin zu Hause.’

rule.name: Change quotation marks inside quotation marks from primary to secondary (“Word: ‘Word’!”)

example.after: à 20,99 CZK à 1 € à 30 Kč

rule.name: Nonbreaking space between value and local currency word (20 dollars)
rule.description: Nonbreaking space between value and local or old currency unit expressed in word: Value – nbspace – local currency word (20 dollars, 10 korun, 1 złoty, 5 euros)

example.before: 5euro (many but not all languages) 20korun (Czech, Slovak) 1000 forint körülbelül 3 dollár, 2 font vagy 63 korona (Hungarian) 20 dollars (English) 100euros (French, Spanish, Portuguese, English) 20 Mark (German) 50 markkaa (Finnish) 15 złotych i 10 groszy (Polish)
example.after: 5 euro (many but not all languages) 20 korun (Czech, Slovak) 1000 forint körülbelül 3 dollár, 2 font vagy 63 korona (Hungarian) 20 dollars (English) 100 euros (French, Spanish, Portuguese, English) 20 Mark (German) 50 markkaa (Finnish) 15 złotych i 10 groszy (Polish)

rule.name: Keep together month and year (e.g., June 56, October 1956, Year 1968)

example.before: Listopad 1989 (Czech) jaro 68 nebo podzim 1989 (Czech) août 99 (French) printemps 1999 (French) April 45 (English, German…) Iunie 1985, Martie‘60, anul2000 (Romanian) Kolovoz 2025. (Croatian) Júl 1999 a jeseň 2000 (Slovak)
example.after: Listopad 1989 (Czech) jaro 68 nebo podzim 1989 (Czech) août 99 (French) printemps 1999 (French) April 45 (English, German…) Iunie 1985, Martie ’60, anul 2000 (Romanian) Kolovoz 2025. (Croatian) Júl 1999 a jeseň 2000 (Slovak)

rule.name: Keep together historical date shorthand (e.g., June ’56, October ’56)
rule.description: The abbreviated version of the year is indicated with a correct apostrophe and separated from the month or season by a non-breaking space to prevent the expression from being split at the end of a line

example.before: Czerwiec ‘56 (Polish) Listopad'89 (Czech, Polish) Roku‘88 (Czech, Polish) août `99 (French) April ´45 (English, German…) Decembrie '89 (Romanian) Anni '80 (Italian) Годината ‘80 (Bulgarian) Október ‘67 (Slovak)
example.after: Czerwiec ’56 (Polish) Listopad ’89 (Czech, Polish) Roku ’88 (Czech, Polish) août ’99 (French) April ’45 (English, German…) Decembrie ’89 (Romanian) Anni ’80 (Italian) Годината ’80 (Bulgarian) Október ’67 (Slovak)

rule.name: Keep date and month name together (2 May)
rule.description: Insert a nonbreaking space in dates in this format: # Month

example.before: 13 ianuarie 2012 (Romanian)
example.after: 13 ianuarie 2012 (Romanian)

rule.name: Keep short dates with periods together without spaces (DMY 12.11.1974)
rule.description: The short date format is written with periods without spaces

rule.name: Keep short dates together without space (27.12.)
rule.description: Keep short dates together without space (27.12.)

rule.name: Keep dates in the format DD MM(Roman numerals) YYYY together
rule.description: Insert a nonbreaking space in dates formatted as DD MM(Roman) YYYY

rule.name: Convert period to preferred separator in dates (slash, hyphen)
rule.description: Convert period to preferred separator in dates DMY (slash, hyphen) – 11/1/2024 or 11-1-2024

example.before: 13.11.1874 13-11-1874 13/11/1874 All separators should be identical
example.after: 13.11.1874 13-11-1874 13/11/1874 All separators should be identical

rule.name: Convert date separator to preferred form in DMY dates
rule.description: Convert date separator to preferred form in dates DMY – 11/1/2024 or 11.1.2024 or 11-1-2024

example.before: 13. 1. 1874 13.11.1874 13-11-1874 13/11/1874 All separators should be identical
example.after: 13.1.1874 13.11.1874 13-11-1874 13/11/1874 All separators should be identical

rule.name: En-dash between date ranges in various formats ending with year (1898 or 89 or ’89)
rule.description: En-dash without spaces between date ranges in various formats (1.2.2020–1.3.2026). Many other forms are supported (1.–2. April 2025, 1. X.–2. XII. or 1. 9.–10. 9. ’87)

rule.name: Fix Dublin 6W instead of incorrect 6 W
rule.description: Fix Dublin 6W instead of incorrect 6 W which means 6 Watt

example.before: The Dublin 6 W designation is unusual.
example.after: The Dublin 6W designation is unusual.

rule.name: Alert: two capital letters at the beginning of a word
rule.description: Two capital letters are not written consecutively at the beginning of a sentence or certain words. However, exceptions may be made for company names, product names, service names, or intentional neologisms.

example.before: EXample of the PRoblem. (Incorrect English) Example of the Problem. (Correct English)

rule.name: Alert: two consecutive identical parentheses or brackets
rule.description: Two identical parentheses in a row are usually incorrect; one of them may be superfluous. However, they may be secondary parentheses, which should have a different form. Or perhaps everything is fine in this particular context.

example.before: (Almost.)) (Incorrect English) (Almost.) (Correct English) ((Almost.) (Incorrect English) (Almost.) (Correct English)

rule.name: Alert: sentence probably starts with lowercase letter
rule.description: The beginning of a sentence should start with a capital letter. However, it is possible that in a given context, the use of a lowercase letter is correct.

example.before: (Hello.) new sentence. (Incorrect English) (Hello.) New sentence. (Correct English) “Hi!” my name is Judy. (Incorrect English) “Hi!” My name is Judy. (Correct English) Filip, Linda atd. jsou kamarádi. (Correct Czech)

rule.name: Alert: a word followed by hyphen
rule.description: A word followed by hyphen could be intentional (Ein- oder Zweizimmerwohnung) or the hyphen could represent dash or hyphen with or without spaces depending on context and language.

example.before: Ein – oder Zweizimmerwohnung (German incorrect) Ein- oder Zweizimmerwohnung (German correct) Nosotros —o tú-. (Spanish incorrect) Nosotros —o tú—. (Spanish correct) Říkáš- li pravdu… (Czech incorrect) Říkáš‑li pravdu… (Czech) budynki jedno- i dwupiętrowe (Polish correct) motywy staro- i nowotestamentowe (Polish correct) kroje jedno- lub dwuelementowe (Polish correct) układy jedno- i wielopoziomowe (Polish correct) reakcje endo- lub egzotermiczne (Polish correct) mono- i poligamia makro- i mikroekonomia elektro- i gazowe

rule.name: Alert: It is possible that this is an incorrectly typed expression “à la”
rule.description: It is possible that this is an incorrectly typed expression “à la” meaning “in the style of”

example.before: Kuře alá bažant (Czech) Kuře á la bažant (Czech) Kuře alà bažant (Czech)

rule.name: Alert: Two initials connected with hyphen
rule.description: Two initials connected by a hyphen can mean “from–to,” in which case they should be written with a dash.

example.before: Dictionary A-Z (English) Slovník A-Ch (Czech)

rule.name: Alert: It is possible that the plus sign (+) is used instead of the † symbol for the date of death.
rule.description: It is possible that the plus sign (+) is used instead of the † symbol for the date of death.

example.before: (* 1928 Budapest, + 2023 Paris) (+2023 in New York) Georges Pompidou (+ 1968) (The spaces between † and year may vary according local preferences.)
example.after: (* 1928 Budapest, † 2023 Paris) (†2023 in New York) Georges Pompidou († 1968) (The spaces between † and year may vary according local preferences.)

rule.name: Keep single-character words together with the following word (prefs)
rule.description: Single-character words at the end of a line may be considered wrong for aestehtic reasons, so they are joined to the following word with a non-breaking space

category.name: Spaces
Single-letter words at the end of a line (prefs)

example.before: A fost la Iași și a vorbit cu o prietenă.
example.after: A fost la Iași și a vorbit cu o prietenă.
